studio: HTTP wait returned the final result (200 with reply)
studio: a stalled consumer does not delay the Run (median with <= 1.5 x median without + 3 s)
studio: a raw TCP consumer (4 KB receive buffer) that joins from the start and never reads is closed with 1013 (slow consumer)

notes: studio: during the live Runs the stalled Node clients were not dropped (8 frames / ~786 SSE bytes piled up): the operating system's socket buffers absorbed them below the server's 1 MB limit. That is a limit of this stimulus, not a verdict; the drop itself is checked below with a raw TCP consumer whose receive buffer is 4 KB.

Chat observers send nothing: the sender is the HTTP POST ?wait=110; WS observers authenticate with the token in the hello (Bearer is only accepted on Studio upgrade). Studio target is the Assistant conversation on the Registry; Product worker conversations need a running pipeline and were not used.

Cursor truth: Chat = GET events?after_cursor=<before> (JSON replay of the journal); Studio = a replayed SSE from the same cursor. Delta text is rebuilt from live deltas; the non-streaming WS observer reads the final text from history after its journal shows the assistant message.

defects.title: Chat never disconnects a stalled consumer: its limit is 160 MB per connection
defects.expected: Spec: a slow consumer is disconnected and reconnects by cursor (Studio does this at 1 MB)
defects.actual: Stalled Chat WS and SSE consumers stayed connected through every Run (4 trials, 0 closes) while 32 frames / 6142 SSE bytes piled up unread. The limit is maxSocketBufferedBytes / maxStreamBufferedBytes, default 160 MB, and index.ts refuses any configured value below MAX_RUNTIME_WEBSOCKET_PAYLOAD_BYTES (160 MB), so it cannot be lowered: each stalled consumer can hold up to 160 MB of Runtime memory before it is dropped; no realistic answer reaches it, so the 1013 / destroy path was not reachable from outside
